comments.author: 00ber
comments.body:
I experienced the same problem today. I had 92% accuracy during training but after loading the saved model, my model's accuracy dropped to like 30%. I retrained the model and checked the before-training and after-training weights of both `model.score.modules_to_save` and `model.score.original_module` and found that the `model.score.original_module` was being updated rather than `model.score.modules_to_save` which is causing the model to use the non-optimized weights after it is loaded.

Until this is fixed, I'm using the following workaround, which seems to work for me (will need to retrain the classifier again though): 

1. Along with the model, save the classification head's state dict separately
```
..........
model.save_pretrained("my-awesome-model")
torch.save(model.score.state_dict(), 'score-params.pt')
```
2. During inference, after loading the peft model, load the saved params into the model's classification head
```
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
from peft import PeftModel, PeftConfig

device_map = "auto"
peft_model_id = "my-awesome-model"
config = PeftConfig.from_pretrained(peft_model_id)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
    config.base_model_name_or_path,
    load_in_8bit=True,
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map=device_map,
    num_labels=3
)
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, peft_model_id)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(config.base_model_name_or_path)
score_params = torch.load('score-params.pt') 
model.score.load_state_dict(score_params)
```

comments.author: linhdvu14
comments.body:
Thanks @00ber for sharing your workaround.

I wonder what is the purpose of `ModulesToSaveWrapper` splitting into `original_module` and `modules_to_save`? Don't you always want to retrain the head i.e. no need for `original_module`?

Aside from this issue, I've also ran into a weird `modules_to_save` error with DeepSpeed zero3. Seems if you initialize DeepSpeed before creating the model (e.g. by using `HfArgumentParser`):
1. `from_pretrained` will partition model params: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v4.30.2/src/transformers/modeling_utils.py#L2666
2. `ModulesToSaveWrapper` will copy the (now empty) `original_module`: https://github.com/huggingface/peft/blob/main/src/peft/utils/other.py#L136
3. The forward pass will `RuntimeError: size mismatch, got XX, XXxYYY,0` as the head is empty

Seems this module might need more testing?

comments.author: 00ber
comments.body: @linhdvu14 I'm not sure of the original purpose behind splitting into original_module and modules_to_save either....But yeah, this module definitely needs a bit more testing it seems. I thought it was an issue just with the sequence classification model, but recently when I tried saving the LM Head for a CausalLM model, I faced a similar issue of the weights not being saved correctly.

comments.author: liuyu666-thu
comments.body:
> @linhdvu14 I'm not sure of the original purpose behind splitting into original_module and modules_to_save either....But yeah, this module definitely needs a bit more testing it seems. I thought it was an issue just with the sequence classification model, but recently when I tried saving the LM Head for a CausalLM model, I faced a similar issue of the weights not being saved correctly.

@00ber @younesbelkada  I met the same weird problem and had a rough conclusion: it is caused by `dispatch_model` function triggered by `load_in_8bit=True` or `device_map is not None`. A AlignDeviceHook may be attached to that causes unexpected module forwarding.

comments.author: BenjaminBossan
comments.body: Hey, thanks everyone here for investigating this bug and providing code to replicate it. We could confirm the error and could pinpoint the issue, the fix is provided in #755. Since this is quite a tricky bug, it would be great if you could help us by checking if the fix solves your original problem.

comments.author: vincentmin
comments.body: @BenjaminBossan Thanks for looking into this issue. For my understanding, could you explain if this fix requires a retraining of our models, or if we can use the adapters from our original training with the old code?

comments.author: vincentmin
comments.body:
I just tried running the following code from @younesbelkada new fix branch:
```
import torch
from peft import PeftModel, PeftConfig
from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer

peft_model_id = "vincentmin/llama-2-7b-reward-oasst1"
config = PeftConfig.from_pretrained(peft_model_id)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
    config.base_model_name_or_path,
    num_labels=1,
    load_in_8bit=True,
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
)
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, peft_model_id)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(config.base_model_name_or_path, use_auth_token=True)
model.eval()
with torch.no_grad():
  test = model(**tokenizer("hello world", return_tensors='pt')).logits
test
```
If I run it twice, I get different results.
Note that the adapters that I load here were created from a training run on the old branch.
I guess that answers my question above: "We cannot use adapters from our original training with the old code".
I can try again tomorrow to see if the issue is fixed if we also train on the new branch.

comments.author: vincentmin
comments.body: @BenjaminBossan I managed to confirm that #755 fixes my issue. I trained in 4bit on the branch #755 and can now consistently load the model with the same model output. Thanks @BenjaminBossan  and @younesbelkada !
